sources.claim: T-SQL logical processing order is FROM, ON, JOIN, WHERE, GROUP BY, WITH CUBE/ROLLUP, HAVING, SELECT, DISTINCT, ORDER BY, TOP; aliases from SELECT can't be referenced by earlier clauses but can by ORDER BY; physical execution may vary
PostgreSQL SELECT evaluation sequence (FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY/HAVING, SELECT list, DISTINCT, set ops, ORDER BY, LIMIT/OFFSET)
PostgreSQL: output column names usable in ORDER BY and GROUP BY but not WHERE or HAVING; name clash resolved opposite ways in ORDER BY vs GROUP BY
Window functions logically execute after WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING and after aggregates; allowed only in SELECT list and ORDER BY
Snowflake: WHERE predicates behave as if evaluated after FROM, optimizer may reorder if results unchanged
DuckDB supports reusable (lateral) column aliases, usable in WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING but not JOIN ON
DuckDB QUALIFY filters window function results, sits after WINDOW and before ORDER BY, can reference SELECT aliases
Worked example and DuckDB alias-in-WHERE behaviour executed locally in DuckDB 1.5.6 (project .venv)

scenes.beat: Hook. Code panel shows the query; SELECT line glows, then visibly drops below the HAVING line.
scenes.narration: You write SELECT first. Logically, SQL processes it after HAVING.

on_screen_text: Logical order. The optimizer may reorder physically.
scenes.beat: Timeline of the 8 logical steps builds left to right. DISTINCT is shown greyed out (this query has no DISTINCT), so the walkthrough numbers 1-7 stay consistent. Small caveat line fades in: this is the logical model, physical execution can differ.
scenes.narration: This is the logical processing order. The optimizer can run things differently, but results must match this model.

scenes.beat: FROM/JOIN clause highlighted. Join matcher links each order to its customer; a 7-row working table appears.
scenes.narration: Step one: FROM and JOIN build the working rows. Seven orders, each matched to a customer.

scenes.beat: WHERE highlighted. Orders 106 (10) and 107 (15) are struck through and fade; 5 rows remain.
scenes.narration: Step two: WHERE filters individual rows. Amounts ten and fifteen are gone.

scenes.beat: GROUP BY highlighted. Surviving rows slide together by name and collapse into 3 group rows with sums.
scenes.narration: Step three: GROUP BY collapses the rows into one per customer.

scenes.beat: HAVING highlighted. Ben's group row is struck through; Asha and Chen remain.
scenes.narration: Step four: HAVING filters groups, not rows. Ben's total is exactly fifty, so he is out.

on_screen_text: ORDER BY can use the alias
scenes.beat: SELECT highlighted; column header becomes 'total'. Then ORDER BY highlighted; rows reorder to Asha 120, Chen 90.
scenes.narration: Step five: SELECT computes the output and names it total. Only then can ORDER BY sort by that alias.

scenes.beat: LIMIT highlighted. Chen's row is struck through; Asha 120 remains as the final result.
scenes.narration: Last, LIMIT one keeps the top row. Asha, one twenty.

code_blocks.code:
SELECT c.name, SUM(o.amount) AS total
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE o.amount >= 20
GROUP BY c.name
HAVING SUM(o.amount) > 50
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 1;
